commons.title: This is an amazing stone wall constructed single-handedly by a man named Tom Hendrix in Florence, Alabama LCCN2010640665.tif
commons.description:
Title: This is an amazing stone wall constructed single-handedly by a man named Tom Hendrix in Florence, Alabama
Physical description: 1 photograph : digital, TIFF file, color.

Notes: Title, date, subject note, and keywords provided by the photographer.; Gift; George F. Landegger; 2010; (DLC/PP-2010:090).; Forms part of the George F. Landegger Collection of Alabama Photographs in Carol M. Highsmith's America Project in the Carol M. Highsmith Archive.; Hendrix's great great grandmother was a 14-year old Yuchi Indian girl who was forcibly moved along with thousands of others to an Oklahoma reservation during the early 1800's. From the reservation she ran away and traveled alone all the way back to her homeland in North Alabama. The stone wall is Hendrix's tribute to her and to all Native American women. He has been working on the wall since 1988.; Credit line: The George F. Landegger Collection of Alabama Photographs in Carol M. Highsmith's America, Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
commons.editorial_reason: The caption mentions a Yuchi ancestor, but the image shows a modern memorial wall built by Tom Hendrix, not Yuchi cultural architecture or an object made by Yuchi people.

commons.title: Indians NW of South Carolina.jpg
commons.description: "Map of the Several Nations of Indians to the Northwest of South Carolina" or the "Catawba Deerskin Map", an annotated copy of hand-painted deerskin original made by a Catawba chieftain to Governor Francis Nicholson"This map describing the scituation [sic] of the several nations of Indians to the NW of South Carolina was coppyed [sic] from a draught [sic] drawn & painted on a deer skin by an Indian Cacique and presented to Francis Nicholason Esqr. Governor of South Carolina by whom it is most humbly dedicated to his Royal Highness George, Prince of Wales."
commons.editorial_reason: This is a historical map, not a visible depiction of Yuchi cultural dress, objects, architecture, music, dance, or craft.
